DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY

[OE Docket No. EA-118-A]

Application To Amend Authorization To Export Electric Energy; 
Hill County Electric Cooperative, Incorporated

AGENCY: Office of Electricity, Department of Energy.

ACTION: Notice of application.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: Hill County Electric Cooperative, Incorporated (the Applicant 
or HCE) has applied to amend its authorization to transmit electric 
energy from the United States to Canada pursuant to the Federal Power 
Act.

DATES: Comments must be submitted on or before December 30, 2026.

ADDRESSES: Comments or requests for more information should be 
addressed by electronic mail to 
[email protected]
.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Marina Fennel, (240) 702-6156, 

[email protected]
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The United States Department of Energy (DOE) 
regulates electricity exports from the United States to foreign 
countries in accordance with section 202(e) of the Federal Power Act 
(FPA) (16 U.S.C. 824a(e)) and regulations thereunder (10 CFR 205.300). 
Sections 301(b) and 402(f) of the DOE Organization Act (42 U.S.C. 
7151(b) and 7172(f)) transferred this regulatory authority, previously 
exercised by the now-defunct Federal Power Commission, to DOE.
    Section 202(e) of the FPA provides that an entity which seeks to 
export electricity must obtain an order from DOE authorizing that 
export (16 U.S.C. 824a(e)). On January 8, 2026, the authority to issue 
such orders was delegated to the DOE's Assistant Secretary for the 
Office of Electricity by Redelegation Order No. S3-DEL-OE1-2026.
    On August 20, 2026, HCE filed an application (Application or App.) 
with DOE for an amendment to their existing export authorization (EA-
118). HCE subsequently submitted a revised application on September 30, 
2026. HCE owns and operates a 69 kV transmission line in Montana that 
serves the Enbridge Inc. (Enbridge) Express Pipeline Ltd. Wildhorse 
pumping station in Alberta, Canada. HCE was issued Presidential Permit 
Docket No. PP-118 and Export Authorization Order No. EA-118 on February 
6, 1997.
    HCE is seeking to increase the total allowable authorized export 
capability over the existing facilities from 6 MW to an instantaneous 
transmission capacity of up to 8 MW. The applicant has received a 
request from Enbridge to increase electrical capacity to facilitate 
potential expansion opportunities at the Wildhorse Facility, thereby 
increasing the capacity of its pipeline into the United States. The 
Applicant performed a load flow analysis and concluded that ``the 
proposed export is within HCE's available system capability and will 
not adversely affect HCE's ability to reliably serve its existing and 
reasonably anticipated native load requirements.'' App. at 2. In 
addition, ``HCE will continue to maintain sufficient resources, 
capacity, and transmission capability to meet its domestic electric 
service obligations. The proposed increase of 2 MW is not expected to 
adversely affect the adequacy or reliability of HCE's system or the 
interconnected electric grid.'' Id. Because the proposed increase is 
under the 4MW or more threshold outlined in the Upper Missouri Zone 
(UMZ) Zonal Planning Criteria, the additional 2MW of growth is not 
considered an unplanned load and does not require balancing authority 
approval for the increase. HCE also ensured that ``the proposed export 
will be conducted in accordance with all applicable interconnection, 
transmission, scheduling, and reliability requirements. HCE does not 
anticipate that the increase from 6 MW to 8 MW will interfere with the 
coordinated use of the U.S. power supply network or adversely affect 
the availability or reliability of electric supply to domestic 
customers.'' Id.
    Procedural Matters: Any person desiring to be heard in this 
proceeding should file a comment to the Application at 

[email protected]
.
    Comments concerning HCE's Application should be clearly marked with 
OE Docket No. EA-118-A. Comments will be posted along with the relevant 
application on the program website at 
www.energy.gov/oe/pending-applications
.
    A final decision will be made on the requested authorization after 
the environmental impacts have been evaluated consistent with the 
National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) of 1969, as amended (42 U.S.C. 
4321, et seq.), the DOE NEPA regulations at 10 CFR part 1021, and the 
DOE's Implementing Procedures (June 2026) and after DOE evaluates 
whether the proposed action will have an adverse impact on the 
sufficiency of supply or reliability of the United States electric 
power supply system.
    Copies of this Application are available on the program website at: 

www.energy.gov/oe/pending-applications
 or by emailing 

[email protected]
.

    Signed in Washington, DC, on November 25, 2026.
Jennifer Hartzell,
